metadata.purpose: Pass 3 remediation: couple the 1D circumferential bilayer mucosal ring constitutive law to a 3D dichotomous bronchial-tree Poiseuille impedance network with heterogeneous airway-smooth-muscle (ASM) activation and Venegas-type flow-stretch feedback, to simulate patchy ventilation defects during asthmatic bronchospasm.
metadata.offline_note: All numbers below were entered from the authors' knowledge of the literature during an isolated (offline) run; DOIs could not be re-verified online. See pass3_citations.bib and the v3 audit references block.

weibel_1963_model_a.source: Weibel ER (1963) Morphometry of the Human Lung, Springer, Berlin (symmetric dichotomous 'model A', generations 0-16 = conducting zone; adult lung at ~3/4 TLC)
weibel_1963_model_a.geometry_note: Half-angle ~35 deg (total bifurcation angle ~70 deg) and alternating ~90 deg rotation of successive bifurcation planes follow the classical Weibel/Horsfield descriptions of the space-filling human bronchial tree; they only affect the 3D rendering, not the impedance network.

air_properties.note: Dry air at ~20 C; body-temperature humidified air has eta ~1.9e-5 Pa s (<5% difference).

poiseuille_network.pressure_unit_conversion: 1 cmH2O s / L = 98066.5 Pa s / m^3
poiseuille_network.limitations: Laminar fully developed Poiseuille flow in every branch; neglects entrance/turbulent losses (Pedley et al. 1970 correction, Re > 2000 in trachea), upper-airway resistance, airway wall compliance and gas inertance. Known consequence: pure Poiseuille Weibel trees place ~40% of conducting-airway resistance in airways < 2 mm, versus ~10-20% measured by Macklem & Mead (1967) retrograde catheter.

healthy_small_airway_resistance_fraction.source: Pure Poiseuille sum over Weibel model A generations 8-16 (d < 2 mm) divided by generations 0-16 total; cross-check of the network against the tabulated geometry (analytic, computed from the rows above).
healthy_small_airway_resistance_fraction.measured_counterpart: Macklem PT & Mead J (1967) J Appl Physiol 22:395-401 report peripheral (< 2 mm) airways contribute < 10-20% of total lower-airway resistance in healthy dog/human lungs (DOI 10.1152/jappl.1967.22.3.395; unverified offline).

homogeneous_constriction_tree_amplificat.source: Exact identity for a series-parallel network whose every branch resistance is scaled by the same factor k (Lean theorem MathOfBiology.Loop_068.bifurcation_resistance_homogeneous_scaling).

venegas_2005_patchiness.source: Venegas JG, Winkler T, Musch G, Vidal Melo MF, Layfield D, Tgavalekos N, Fischman AJ, Callahan RJ, Bellardine C, Harris RS (2005) Self-organized patchiness in asthma as a prelude to catastrophic shifts. Nature 434:777-782
venegas_2005_patchiness.ventilation_defect_definition: Terminal units receiving < 50% of the tree-mean ventilation at fixed tidal volume (model definition; Venegas et al. threshold PET-measured specific ventilation at a comparable fraction of the lung mean).
qualitative_predictions: Ventilation defects in asthma are large, contiguous (clustered) and bistable, emerging from positive feedback between reduced tidal stretch and increased ASM shortening.
Defects self-organize above a critical ASM activation / feedback gain; below it ventilation stays nearly uniform (catastrophic shift).
Defect fraction of total lung during bronchoconstriction challenge in mild asthmatics was reported at ~20-40% of imaged lung volume (PET 13NN washout).

wiggs_1992_whole_lung_amplification.source: Wiggs BR, Bosken C, Pare PD, James A, Hogg JC (1992) A model of airway narrowing in asthma and in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Am Rev Respir Dis 145:1251-1258
wiggs_1992_whole_lung_amplification.note: Thickened asthmatic airway walls amplify the whole-lung resistance response to a given ASM shortening by roughly an order of magnitude relative to normal walls at ~30-40% shortening (computed on a Weibel/Horsfield tree).
wiggs_1992_whole_lung_amplification.reference_tree_amplification_note: 3.66 = 16.52 / 4.51, the single-airway Poiseuille ratio in airway_mucosal_creasing_reference.json; exact for homogeneous constriction, lower bound reference for heterogeneous constriction.

heterogeneity_model.asm_strain_distribution: epsilon_i^(0) = clip(epsilon_mean * exp(sigma * xi_i - sigma^2 / 2), 0, epsilon_max), xi_i ~ N(0,1) i.i.d. per branch (log-normal, mean-preserving)
heterogeneity_model.sigma_note: Assumed 10% branch-to-branch coefficient of variation of ASM activation (no direct measurement available offline). With sigma = 0.10 and kappa = 0 the healthy tree shows ~1% ventilation defects, i.e. an essentially uniform baseline.
heterogeneity_model.boundary_condition: fixed tidal volume (flow-controlled breathing): tidal stretch of branch i is Q_i / mean_g(Q) with mean_g the mean flow of its generation; whole-lung resistance R_tree is reported at that fixed flow (Venegas et al. 2005 modelling assumption)
heterogeneity_model.feedback_rule: epsilon_i <- clip(epsilon_i^(0) * (1 + gain_i * tanh(1 - Q_i / mean_g(Q))), 0, epsilon_max) with gain_i = kappa when Q_i < mean_g(Q) (loss of tidal stretch increases ASM shortening) and gain_i = dilation_gain_ratio * kappa when Q_i > mean_g(Q); under-relaxed fixed-point iteration epsilon <- (1 - omega) epsilon + omega epsilon_target (Venegas et al. 2005 flow-stretch positive feedback, saturating form)
heterogeneity_model.kappa_calibration: kappa_default is the largest gain in kappa_sweep for which the Healthy Bronchiole tree at epsilon_mean = 0.28 keeps its ventilation-defect fraction below 5% (calibrated on the healthy control only); the Severe Asthma defect fraction at the same kappa is then a prediction compared against Venegas et al. (2005).
heterogeneity_model.mucosal_thickness_scaling: h_m / R_0 held at the phenotype value (11.2/600 healthy, 19.1/600 bronchitis, 31.8/600 asthma) across generations, so that m* is generation-independent (Wiggs et al. 1997: wall area scales with perimeter^2 across the tree).
